AI chatbots are legacy technology now.

This week confirmed what the sharpest enterprise teams already knew: the real shift is not smarter chat interfaces. It is persistent autonomous agents — AI systems that hold context across sessions, execute multi-step workflows, and operate independently inside your business.

The evidence is concrete. Claude Opus 5 is being used for full enterprise codebase migrations — not suggestions, not autocomplete, but end-to-end migration workflows. Microsoft shipped agent inventory tracking and kill-switch governance on August 18. When the largest software company on Earth builds an off-switch for AI agents, it is because those agents are already running live in production at enterprise scale.

This changes the executive conversation entirely. The question is no longer whether AI is useful. It is whether your organization has the governance and architecture to manage autonomous systems that act on your behalf across code, operations, and customer workflows simultaneously.
